title: Machine-learned multiscale simulations reveal lipid-dependent RAS organization at membranes
summary: The MuMMI machine-learning multiscale simulation ensemble found that local membrane lipid fingerprints correlate with wild-type KRAS clustering and orientation, with many simulated RAS–RAS interfaces appearing nonspecific. Complementary liposome and diffusion experiments supported lipid-dependent RAS adhesion and dynamics, motivating the authors' conclusion that lipids can mediate RAS multimer organization.
organization: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory; Los Alamos National Laboratory, and the NCI RAS Initiative

evidence.tested: Complementary liposome and diffusion experiments supported lipid-dependent RAS adhesion and dynamics, motivating the authors' conclusion that lipids can mediate RAS multimer organization.
evidence.unknown: Most specific orientation and interface conclusions are simulation-derived; experimental comparisons provide validation of selected membrane adhesion/diffusion behaviors, not direct demonstration of these mechanisms in intact cells or cancer outcomes. Authors describe absolute diffusion values as semiquantitative and dependent on methods/force fields.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning selects diverse local membrane patches from a macroscale lipid model to launch and couple atomistic/coarse-grained simulations, producing an ensemble of more than 100,000 simulations. The resulting simulations identified lipid-composition relationships with RAS orientation and multimer organization; selected predictions were compared with surface-plasmon resonance, fluorescence-correlation and other biophysical experiments.
